name: Clear screen bitmap (LDIR)
code:
ld hl,$4000
    ld (hl),0
    ld de,$4001
    ld bc,6143
    ldir

name: Set all attributes
code:
ld hl,$5800
    ld (hl),%00111000   ; white paper, black ink
    ld de,$5801
    ld bc,767
    ldir

name: Random border stripes
code:
stripes:
    ld a,r
    and 7
    out ($FE),a
    jr stripes

name: Install bold font
code:
; Embolden the ROM font into fontbuf, then point CHARS at it
    ld hl,$3D00          ; ROM character set
    ld de,fontbuf
boldloop:
    ld a,(hl)
    ld c,a
    srl a                ; copy each set pixel to the one on its right
    or c
    ld (de),a
    inc hl
    inc de
    ld a,h
    cp $40               ; stop at $4000 (768 bytes done)
    jr nz,boldloop
    ld hl,fontbuf-256    ; CHARS = font base - 256 (space is code 32)
    ld ($5C36),hl
    ret
fontbuf:
    ds 768

name: Wait for any key
code:
waitkey:
    xor a                ; scan all keyboard half-rows
    in a,($FE)
    and 31
    cp 31                ; 31 = nothing pressed
    jr z,waitkey

name: Macro: simple
code:
; A macro is a block of source given a name. Calling the name pastes
; the block in — nothing is called at runtime, so there is no RET and
; no stack cost, but every call costs its bytes again.

    macro PUSHALL           ; no parameters: the plainest form
        push af
        push bc
        push de
        push hl
        push ix
        push iy
        ex af,af'
        exx                 ; from here the alternate set is the live one
        push af
        push bc
        push de
        push hl
    endm

    macro POPALL            ; the mirror image, popped in reverse
        pop hl
        pop de
        pop bc
        pop af
        ex af,af'
        exx
        pop iy
        pop ix
        pop hl
        pop de
        pop bc
        pop af
    endm

isr:
    PUSHALL
    ld a,2
    out ($FE),a             ; whatever the interrupt has to do
    POPALL
    ei
    reti

name: Macro: with parameters
code:
; Parameters are substituted as text, so an argument can be any
; expression the assembler can work out. The trailing '?' is the
; sjasmplus convention that keeps a parameter name from colliding
; with a label of the same name.

    macro BORDER colour?
        ld a,colour?
        out ($FE),a
    endm

    macro FILLATTR attr?        ; paint the whole attribute area
        ld hl,$5800
        ld (hl),attr?
        ld de,$5801
        ld bc,767
        ldir
    endm

start:
    BORDER 2                    ; red
    FILLATTR %01000110          ; bright yellow ink on black paper
    BORDER 7 - 2                ; an expression is fine: it pastes "7 - 2"
    ret

name: Macro: with a loop counter
code:
; REPT repeats a block; a second operand names a counter that runs
; 0..count-1 inside it, so one block can generate a whole table.
; (DUP/EDUP is the same thing under its other name.)

    macro SCRTABLE rows?
        rept rows?, y       ; y = 0,1,2,... within the block
            dw $4000 + (y & 192) * 32 + (y & 7) * 256 + (y & 56) * 4
        endr
    endm

    macro UNROLL_LDI n?     ; a counter is optional — plain REPT unrolls
        rept n?
            ldi
        endr
    endm

linetab:
    SCRTABLE 192            ; 192 screen-line addresses, 384 bytes

copy8:
    UNROLL_LDI 8            ; eight LDIs, no loop overhead
    ret

name: Macro: with internal labels
code:
; A plain label inside a macro is defined again on every call, so the
; second call fails with "label already defined". A label starting with
; a dot is local to the expansion — each call gets its own.

    macro DELAY loops?
        ld b,loops?
.wait:                      ; local: only this expansion sees it
        djnz .wait
    endm

    macro CLAMP max?        ; A = min(A, max?)
        cp max? + 1
        jr c,.done
        ld a,max?
.done:
    endm

start:
    DELAY 50
    DELAY 200               ; same macro again, no clash
    ld a,40
    CLAMP 31
    CLAMP 15
    ret
